findings.claim: Processing requests store a fixed input range.
findings.evidence: The table says "Fixed input range". Requests do persist an explicit ByteRange (src/model/request.rs:12), but the range is not fixed for the lifetime of a request. The real producer Transcripts::create_request_for_range reads the transcript and commits bookkeeping.request_create with an explicit range (src/transcripts/mod.rs:286-307). RequestCreate::apply selects overlapping pending requests (src/transcripts/mutations.rs:375-379), preserves the oldest request ID, expands keeper.range to the union, and writes that same requests/<id>.toml again (src/transcripts/mutations.rs:387-404). Thus a pending request for [0,100) can become [0,200) when a later explicit [50,200) request is created; merged peers become unresolved. The delivery consumer subsequently reads the updated rq.range (src/transcripts/delivery.rs:83-103). The range is fixed after delivery because merge candidates are restricted to Pending, so the high-level claim could be made accurate by qualifying that lifecycle boundary.
